stem: In the chest X-ray, the increased density in the right lower zone represents consolidation in which lobe? (Refer to Case 5)

options.text: Basal segment of right upper lobe

explanation: A right lower-zone opacity on chest X-ray most commonly localises to the right lower lobe, particularly when the silhouette sign helps identify adjacent structures and lobar anatomy.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Chest X-Ray - Part B

optionExplanations.A: The basal segment of the right upper lobe is anatomically superior and does not usually produce a right lower-zone opacity.
optionExplanations.B: Right middle lobe consolidation typically causes loss of the right heart border rather than a lower-zone opacity.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: a right lower-zone increased density is most consistent with right lower lobe consolidation.

The following text applies to the questions at positions 13, 14, 15, 16, 17

Instructions

Questions 13 -17 relate to Case 5

Case 5

Various structures are visible on the chest radiograph because of the density difference between them and the anatomically adjacent aerated lung. The replacement of alveolar air by soft tissue density, such as secretions, inflammatory fluid or oedema, will remove the density gradient and the borders will no longer be distinguishable, known as the silhouette sign.

It is important to understand the lobar anatomy and thus the location of infection when interpreting the radiograph. The following five questions will help you practise this skill.
